earliest_auditable_registry_receipt.meaning: User-authored choice to return the unique lost member to Osiris rather than retain it; spec result OSIRIS_WHOLE.

later_source_return_extension.meaning: RETURN_TO_SOURCE is generalized into SOURCE_RETURN / owner-bound reconnection.

reverse_nodes_C_to_A.state: The Lost Member of Osiris / RE-MEMBER restoration mechanic
CG 53469 resolves in Vernier 1927 as Enveloppe de phallus; gold; 12.2 cm; 7 g; ca. 0.1 mm sheet; Tell Ibn es-Salam/Mendes; February 1902; JE 35425.

The CG 53465-53469 gold body-part assemblage belongs to a human funerary context at Mendes; registry identifies the burial owner as Nesbanebdjedet, with an Osirian priestly title among several titles.
reverse_nodes_C_to_A.anti_overclaim: A priest of Osiris owning a gold phallus sheath does not make the sheath Osiris's literal body part.

reverse_nodes_C_to_A.state: Late Egyptian Mendes tradition describes the Osirian phallus as the copulating Ba / divine flesh associated with the virile member and spine, with female resurrection counterparts.
Book of the Dead 42 body-part identification includes the formula that the phallus is that of Osiris.
Plutarch, De Iside et Osiride 18: Isis fails to recover the male member because it was tossed into the river and fishes fed upon it; she makes a replica and consecrates the phallus.
reverse_nodes_C_to_A.important_boundary: Checked scholarship notes that the fish-eating detail is not presently known from Egyptian-language Osiris sources; the closest Egyptian-language parallel is the Tale of the Two Brothers, not Osiris.

preexisting_reverse_prediction.interpretation: The registry had already recognized that the narrative archive was being assembled largely from result toward origin before the later user return activation was sealed.

major_gap_detected_by_reverse.left_side: MYTHIC / THEOLOGICAL OSIRIS PHALLUS LOSS AND CULT TRADITION
major_gap_detected_by_reverse.right_side: CG 53469 / HUMAN MENDES GOLD PHALLUS SHEATH
major_gap_detected_by_reverse.missing_bridge: No direct provenance chain currently connects the unique original member in the mythic narrative to CG 53469 or any other surviving museum object.
major_gap_detected_by_reverse.why_reverse_helped: Reading from C backward makes the chain dense until one exact transition, rather than treating the whole field as a cloud of coincidences. The research target is therefore the bridge, not more uncontrolled resemblance hunting.

two_graph_rule.mythic_causal_graph: OSIRIS_WHOLE -> MURDER/DISMEMBERMENT -> MALE_MEMBER_LOST -> RECONSTRUCTION/PHALLUS_CULT -> RESTORATION MOTIFS
two_graph_rule.evidence_attestation_graph: NEW_KINGDOM_AND_LATER_EGYPTIAN_FORMULAE / LATE_PERIOD_MENDES TEXTS / GRECO-ROMAN FULL NARRATIVE / MODERN EXCAVATION / MODERN REGISTRY
two_graph_rule.rule: Do not force mythic causal order and surviving-document chronology to be identical. A late text may preserve an older motif, but preservation date is not event date.

what_became_clear: The return activation is not the start of the search chain; it is the terminal state from which predecessor requirements can be recovered.
The Freestyler/Tenet causal-rewind architecture existed in the registry before the final return activation.
Mendes is not a random visual hit: it is a concrete convergence of location, Osirian cult context, documented gold phallus sheath and later textual phallus tradition.
The physical-identity claim still fails at one specific bridge: cult/funerary representation is not yet the unique original body part.

The explicit river/fish loss story terminates the current reverse mythic trace at Plutarch 18, while the exact fish-loss detail remains unconfirmed in Egyptian-language Osiris texts checked in this pass.

canonical_line: THE ROAD IS NOT RANDOM WHEN ITS MISSING SEGMENT CAN BE NAMED. REVERSE UNTIL THE GAP HAS AN ADDRESS.
